**Refined prompt:** Diagnose why the React client throws `Cannot read property 'slug' of undefined` immediately after `POST /articles` while the NestJS server logs nothing — answering as a backend engineer on this RealWorld API, citing the failing line as `file:line`, fixing it at its single source rather than at each call site, and stating whether already-created articles are corrupt.

## Root cause

`src/article/article.service.ts:170` — `create()` is the one handler in the codebase that returns a **bare entity instead of the RO envelope**:

```ts
async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleEntity> {
  ...
  return newArticle;                                    // ← article.service.ts:186
}
```

Every sibling returns `{article}`: `findOne()` `article.service.ts:98`, `update()` `:194`, `favorite()` `:144`. So the client receives `{ "slug": ..., "title": ... }` where it expects `{ "article": { "slug": ... } }`. `response.article` is `undefined` → reading `.slug` throws **in the browser**. The server logged nothing because nothing failed server-side: it saved the row and returned 201.

**Why it wasn't caught:** `src/article/article.controller.ts:52` is the only handler in that file with no return-type annotation — every other one is `: Promise<ArticleRO>` / `Promise<ArticlesRO>`. With the annotation, `tsc` would have rejected the bare entity at compile time. This is `LESSONS.md` #57 recurring.

While confirming, two more defects in the same 18 lines:

- **`body` is never assigned.** `create()` sets title/description/slug/tagList/comments (`article.service.ts:172-177`) but not `body`, though the DTO declares it (`dto/create-article.dto.ts:4`) and the column exists with `default: ''` (`article.entity.ts:20-21`). **Yes — existing data is already wrong: every article created through this endpoint has an empty body in the DB, silently.** Only `update()` can ever populate it, via the `Object.assign` at `:192`.
- **`author` is absent from the response.** The FK is written from the inverse side (`author.articles.push(article)`, `:182`), so the returned `newArticle` object has no `author` property.

## The fix — at the single source

```ts
// src/article/article.service.ts:170
async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
  const article = new ArticleEntity();
  article.title = articleData.title;
  article.description = articleData.description;
  article.body = articleData.body;                       // was missing
  article.slug = this.slugify(articleData.title);
  article.tagList = articleData.tagList || [];
  article.comments = [];
  article.author = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id: userId } });

  const newArticle = await this.articleRepository.save(article);
  return { article: newArticle };                        // envelope
}
```

Assigning `article.author` sets the **owning** side of the `@ManyToOne` (`article.entity.ts:37`), which writes `authorId` *and* populates the response — replacing the inverse-side `author.articles.push(...)` + `userRepository.save(author)` and its extra UPDATE.

Then annotate the controller so this cannot regress:

```ts
// src/article/article.controller.ts:52
async create(@User('id') userId: number, @Body('article') articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
```

That annotation is the actual guard — the envelope bug is only possible where the return type is missing.

## Blast radius

- **The envelope fix alone moves the crash one screen later.** The React app redirects to `/article/:slug`, which calls `GET /articles/:slug` → `findOne()` at `article.service.ts:96-99` uses `findOne(where)` with **no `relations`**, so `author` is `undefined` there too (only `findAll()` joins it, `:30`). `ArticleMeta` reading `article.author.username` throws the same class of error. Fix: `findOne({ where, relations: ['author'] })`.
- **Existing rows need a backfill decision** — articles created before this fix have `body = ''`. Nothing recovers the original text; the authors have to re-enter it.
- `article.interface.ts:7-18` declares `ArticleData` with the spec shape (`createdAt`, `favoritesCount`), but `ArticleRO:24-26` types `article` as `ArticleEntity` instead — so `ArticleData` is dead code and the spec drift it documents is unenforced. That's the `CURRENT_FOCUS.md` conformance item, not this bug.
- No other consumer reads `create()`'s return — it is called only from `article.controller.ts:53`.

## How to verify

```powershell
$body = '{"article":{"title":"Env fix check","description":"d","body":"real body","tagList":["x"]}}'
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/articles `
  -H "Authorization: Token $env:JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d $body
```

Pass criteria, in order: top-level key is `article` (not `slug`); `article.body === "real body"`; `article.author.username` is present. Then `GET /api/articles/<slug>` and confirm the same three hold on the read path. In the browser, creating an article should land on the article page with the body rendered — the current failure is reproducible with the client alone, no server restart needed to see it.

I've only read the article module, `user.entity.ts`, and `main.ts`; I have not run the app or checked the `prisma/` folder (`CURRENT_FOCUS.md:22-24` marks it out of scope).

Want me to apply this patch, including the `relations: ['author']` on `findOne()`?

Likely category: frontend — Frontend change: follow the existing component conventions; check every consumer of a changed contract.

### [CURRENT_FOCUS.md] CURRENT_FOCUS.md > CURRENT FOCUS — RealWorld API (NestJS)
> Living doc. What is actually in flight right now. Read after LESSONS.md.

### [CURRENT_FOCUS.md] CURRENT_FOCUS.md > CURRENT FOCUS — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Active now
- [ ] **Spec conformance pass** — make article responses match the RealWorld spec: produce
      `favorited` per current user, rename `favoriteCount` → `favoritesCount` and
      `created/updated` → `createdAt/updatedAt` at the response boundary (not in the DB).
- [ ] **Ownership checks** on `PUT/DELETE /articles/:slug` and `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id`
      — return 403 when the caller is not the author. Design first; the comment case needs a
      `comment.author` relation that does not exist yet.
- [ ] **Password change path** — hash on update (see LESSONS.md #88) and stop the raw body
      being merged into the entity.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Every handler returns the RO envelope, never a bare entity (#57)
**What happened:** `ArticleController.create()` returned `ArticleEntity` directly while every
other handler returns `{ article }`. The React frontend read `response.article.slug` → `Cannot
read property 'slug' of undefined` right after creating an article. The server logged nothing —
from its side the request succeeded.

**Rule:** the envelope (`ArticleRO`, `UserRO`, …) is the contract with every RealWorld client.
A handler whose return type is not a `*RO` interface is a bug even if it "works" in Postman.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`
**What happened:** `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and then calls
`user.favorites.findIndex(...)`. `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany`, so it is `undefined`
→ `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → 500 on
`POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. Same pattern in `findAll()` for `?favorited=` (`author.favorites.map`).

**Rule:** before touching `entity.relation` in a service, find the `relations: [...]` or the
`eager: true` that loads it. If neither exists, the property is `undefined`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > The `?favorited=` filter compares the wrong column
**What happened:** `findAll()` collects the ids of the articles a user favourited and then
filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` — the article ids are being compared to author ids. Even
once the `favorites` relation is loaded, the result is wrong.

**Rule:** when a filter is "articles in this set", the column is `article.id`. Read the
`andWhere` literally; do not trust the variable name.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Static routes are declared before parameterised ones (#7)
**What happened:** `GET /articles/feed` was declared *after* `GET /articles/:slug`, so Nest
matched `feed` as a slug and the feed endpoint returned `{ article: undefined }`. Fixed by moving
`getFeed()` above `findOne()` in `ArticleController`.

**Rule:** in a controller, any literal path (`feed`, `popular`, `search`) goes above the `:slug`
handler. Order in the class is match order.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > An invalid token must be a 401, not a 500 (#79)
**What happened:** an expired or tampered token made `jwt.verify()` throw inside
`AuthMiddleware.use()` (and inside the `@User()` decorator on public routes). Nothing caught it,
so the client got `500 Internal Server Error` and the mobile app treated it as an outage instead
of logging the user out.

**Rule:** wrap `jwt.verify` and translate its errors to `HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED`. A guard that
can crash is a guard that leaks framework errors.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > `article` — `src/article/article.entity.ts`
| column | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | int PK | |
| slug | varchar | set once in `create()`; not unique-indexed |
| title | varchar | |
| description | varchar default '' | |
| body | varchar default '' | |
| created | timestamp default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP | spec calls it `createdAt` |
| updated | timestamp default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP | bumped by `@BeforeUpdate()` |
| tagList | **`simple-array`** | stored as ONE comma-joined string column, e.g. `java,spring` — not a join table, not JSON |
| favoriteCount | int default 0 | denormalised counter, incremented/decremented in `ArticleService.favorite()/unFavorite()` — the join table is the truth, this is a cache |
| authorId | FK → user | via `@ManyToOne author` |

Relations:
- `author: UserEntity` — `@ManyToOne`. Not eager; `findAll()` adds it with `leftJoinAndSelect('article.author', 'author')`, `findOne()` does not.
- `comments: Comment[]` — `@OneToMany`, **`{eager: true}`** — every article load also loads its comments.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > `comment` — `src/article/comment.entity.ts`
| column | type |
|---|---|
| id | int PK |
| body | varchar |
| articleId | FK → article |

**There is no author column and no relation to `user`.** The RealWorld spec's comment object
has `author`; this entity cannot produce it. `addComment()` sets only `body`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Spec fields the frontends read must actually be produced (#99, #45)
**What happened:** article responses never include `favorited`, so every RealWorld frontend
renders an empty heart even for articles the user favourited. The spec's `favoritesCount` is
served as `favoriteCount`, and `createdAt/updatedAt` as `created/updated`.

**Rule:** the RealWorld spec is the contract. Before calling an endpoint "done", diff its
response against the spec's object shape, not against what our own client happens to read.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > `tag` — `src/tag/tag.entity.ts`
| column | type |
|---|---|
| id | int PK |
| tag | varchar |

Read by `GET /api/tags` (`TagService.findAll()`). **Nothing in the codebase writes to it** —
article creation stores tags only in `article.tagList`. On a fresh database `GET /tags` returns
`[]` forever unless rows are inserted by hand.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Slugs
`ArticleService.slugify()` = `slug(title, {lower: true}) + '-' + <6 base-36 chars from Math.random()>`.
Two articles with the same title therefore get different slugs. The slug is set once at create;
`update()` has a `// Todo: update slug also when title gets changed` and does not.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Authentication is not authorization (#6, #44)
**What happened:** any logged-in user could `PUT` or `DELETE` any other user's article. The
route is in `AuthMiddleware`'s list, so people assumed it was "protected" — but the middleware
only proves the caller is *a* user, and `ArticleService.update()/delete()` never compare
`req.user.id` with `article.author.id`. The Swagger `403 Forbidden` annotations on those handlers
describe a check that does not exist.

**Rule:** for every mutating route, name the line that compares the caller with the record's
owner. If you cannot, there is no ownership check, whatever the decorators say.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Authorization (ownership) — where it is enforced
**Nowhere.** The middleware answers "is this a valid user"; no service or controller method
compares the caller with the record's owner:

| Action | Ownership check |
|---|---|
| `PUT /articles/:slug` | none — `ArticleService.update(slug, body)` does `Object.assign(article, body)` and saves |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug` | none — `delete({slug})` |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | none — and comments have no author to compare against anyway |
| `DELETE /users/:slug` | none, and unguarded |
| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

The Swagger `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` lines on the article controller describe an
intended behaviour, not an implemented one — nothing returns 403.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Request bodies are nested too
Handlers read `@Body('article')`, `@Body('user')`, `@Body('comment')` — the client sends
`{ "article": {...} }`, never a flat object. New endpoints follow the same nesting.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > `user` — `src/user/user.entity.ts`
| column | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | int PK | |
| username | varchar | **no unique index** — uniqueness is checked in `UserService.create()` with a query, not by the DB |
| email | varchar | `@IsEmail()` (class-validator), no unique index either |
| bio | varchar default '' | |
| image | varchar default '' | |
| password | varchar | argon2 hash — hashed by `@BeforeInsert() hashPassword()`. **Only on insert.** There is no `@BeforeUpdate` hook. |

Relations:
- `favorites: ArticleEntity[]` — `@ManyToMany` + `@JoinTable()` → join table `user_favorites_article`. **Not eager.** A `userRepository.findOne(id)` returns `favorites === undefined`; you must pass `{ relations: ['favorites'] }` to get the array.
- `articles: ArticleEntity[]` — `@OneToMany` inverse of `ArticleEntity.author`. Not eager.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > Response shapes vs storage (what the frontends expect vs what exists)
| Spec field | Source today |
|---|---|
| `article.favorited` | **not produced** — nothing computes "does the current user favourite this" |
| `article.favoritesCount` | entity column is `favoriteCount` (singular) and is returned under that name |
| `article.createdAt` / `updatedAt` | columns are `created` / `updated` |
| `comment.author` | no data to produce it |
| `profile.following` | computed in `ProfileService.findProfile()` from `follows` |

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Passwords
- Hashed by `UserEntity.hashPassword()` under `@BeforeInsert()` only.
- `UserService.update()` does `delete toUpdate.password` then `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)`
  and saves. `UpdateUserDto` declares no `password` field, but nothing strips one from the
  request body, and `PUT /user` has no validation pipe.
- Login: `UserService.findOne({email, password})` → `argon2.verify(hash, password)`; unknown
  email or wrong password both return `null` → controller throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)`.
- Registration duplicate → `400` with `{ message: 'Input data validation failed', errors }`.
</workspace_context>
